sections.h2: Who appraises and bills property tax in Midland, TX?
sections.html:
In Midland the Midland Central Appraisal District sets values and also mails the tax bills for Midland County property. Its office is at 4631 Andrews Hwy, Midland, TX 79703, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and the main phone is 432-699-4991.

The district's news page reports that it mailed an estimated 548,842 bills for the 2026 tax year on October 23, 2026. If your parcel lies in Martin County instead of Midland County, ask the Martin County tax office which office bills it.

Texas has no state property tax. The appraisal district values each parcel as of January 1, the Appraisal Review Board hears disputes, and each city, school, county and special district sets its own rate. Midland CAD's own FAQ describes the same chain: the district appraises, the board settles disagreements, and the taxing units set budgets and rates.

sections.h2: What are the Midland tax rates for 2025 and 2026?
sections.html:
The City of Midland's rate rose from $0.347999 per $100 in the 2025 tax year to $0.383092 for 2026, according to the appraisal district's rate page. Your bill adds the school district, county, college and hospital district to the city's share.

sections.h2: When are Midland property taxes due?
sections.html:
Midland taxes are due when you get the statement, and they stay penalty-free through January 31 of the next year. The district's FAQ says collections begin around October 1 and that penalty and interest start on February 1.

The Texas Comptroller spells out the cost of waiting: a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest on February 1, then 1 percent more penalty each month until July 1, when the penalty reaches 12 percent. Interest continues at 1 percent a month. Attorney fees of up to 20 percent can be added after that.

  • Over-65 and disabled homeowners can pay in four installments.
  • Some collectors allow a payment plan of up to 36 months on delinquent tax, and the law requires one only for a residence homestead.
  • A written request to waive penalty and interest must be made before the 181st day after the delinquency date, and the tax generally has to be paid within 21 days of learning of the delinquency.

The district also notes that, because pennies are unavailable, it accepts exact change, checks or credit cards for payment. Bring the account number from your statement when you pay in person, and keep the receipt in your closing file if you sell later that year.

sections.h2: Which exemptions apply to a Midland home?
sections.html:
A Midland homestead gets $140,000 off the value for Midland ISD taxes, and the city does not list a general homestead exemption, per the appraisal district's exemption page. Where the city does help is for older owners: the page shows $8,000 for homeowners 65 or older.

  • Over-65 amounts shown: Midland County $150,000, City of Midland $8,000, Midland Hospital $20,000, Midland College $8,000, and Midland ISD $60,000.
  • Disability amounts shown: Midland County $150,000 and Midland ISD $60,000.
  • A homeowner may claim either the disability or the over-65 exemption, but not both, and the district says the over-65 one is better.
  • Midland County's local homestead option is listed at 3 percent with a $5,000 minimum, with $0 granted in the table.
  • Disabled veterans receive up to $5,000, $7,500, $10,000 or $12,000 depending on rating, and a 100 percent rating covers the full homesteadable value.

Exemptions follow the January 1 owner. If you bought after that date, you must file your own application. A late homestead application is accepted up to one year after the tax becomes delinquent, and a 65-year-old owner can apply any time in the birthday year and get the exemption for the full year.

sections.h2: How do I protest a Midland appraisal?
sections.html:
The district says its notices of appraised value usually arrive in mid-April, and a protest is due by May 15 or 30 days after notice delivery, whichever is later, under Texas law. The Comptroller lists April 1 as the target for homestead notices, so a Midland owner should watch the mail from early April.

If the Appraisal Review Board rules against you, the next steps are district court, binding arbitration, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the board value tops $1,000,000. Pay at least the undisputed tax by the delinquency date while you appeal.

The district's FAQ says the notice describes the property, gives its value and exemptions, and estimates the tax. It also says values change when sales data moves or when a record is corrected for square footage or a pool, so read the description line by line for errors before you decide whether to protest.

The homestead cap limits growth in appraised value to 10 percent a year on a qualified homestead, starting the year after the exemption is first granted. The district can reappraise every year, and it must reappraise each property at least once every three years.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Midland?
sections.html:
Midland grew quickly: the Census Bureau estimated 147,615 residents on July 1, 2025, compared with 132,524 in the 2020 census and 111,147 in 2010. That is an 11.1 percent rise since April 2020 on the Bureau's estimates base.

For 2020 through 2024, owners lived in 65.1 percent of homes, and the median owner-occupied home was valued at $319,200. Median owner costs were $2,205 a month with a mortgage and $766 without one, median gross rent was $1,434, and median household income was $89,585. The city has 53,414 households and covers 75.45 square miles of land, with about 1,756 people per square mile in 2020. Residents 65 or older make up 10.1 percent of the population.

sections.h2: What should a Midland seller do about property tax?
sections.html:
Check the current balance on the Midland CAD account before you list, since the district both appraises and bills. A lien attaches on January 1 of each year, and the owner on that date is liable for that year's tax even after a sale.

  • Ask the title company how the current year's tax will be prorated.
  • Tell the buyer to file their own homestead application, because the exemption on file belongs to the January 1 owner.
  • If taxes are already delinquent, request a payoff figure that includes penalty, interest and any attorney fee.
  • If you inherited the house, heirs not named on a recorded deed give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill to claim the homestead exemption.

faqs.q: What is the City of Midland property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's rate is $0.383092 per $100 of taxable value for the 2026 tax year, up from $0.347999 for 2025, per the Midland Central Appraisal District. Midland ISD, the county, the college and the hospital district add their own rates.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Midland County property taxes?
faqs.a: The Midland Central Appraisal District mails the bills and takes payments at 4631 Andrews Hwy, Midland, phone 432-699-4991. Parcels in Martin County should ask the Martin County tax office.

faqs.q: Does the City of Midland give a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The appraisal district's exemption page lists no general homestead exemption for the city, only $8,000 for owners 65 or older. Midland ISD grants $140,000 on a homestead.

faqs.q: Can I get a homestead exemption late?
faqs.a: Yes. The district says you can file a late homestead application up to one year after the taxes become delinquent, but you must file it, since exemptions do not carry over from the previous owner.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Midland property tax by January 31?
faqs.a: Texas adds a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest on February 1, and the penalty grows to 12 percent by July 1. Attorney fees of up to 20 percent may follow.
